title: Braised Potatoes
summary: Potatoes simmered in a soy sauce braise until glossy. Shaving the sharp edges off the pieces keeps them from breaking up.
intro:
If the braising liquid turns cloudy and the potatoes collapse, the likely reasons are that they were not soaked to draw out the starch, or that the heat was too high from the start.

Cook them slowly over medium-low heat with the lid on, and only raise the heat at the end to bring up the gloss.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Trim the sharp corners lightly with a knife and they will hold together better as they cook.
Soak them in cold water for 10 minutes to draw out the starch, then lift them into a sieve and shake off the water.
Cut the onion and carrot into pieces about the same size as the potatoes.
Heat the cooking oil in a pot and stir-fry the potatoes over medium heat for 3 minutes. The surfaces will turn slightly translucent.
Add 300 mL (1 1/4 cups) water, the soy sauce and the sugar, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once it boils, turn the heat down to medium-low, cover, and braise for 12 minutes. Do not stir during this time.
Add the carrot, onion and minced garlic, take the lid off and braise for 5 minutes more.
When about a quarter of the liquid is left, add the oligosaccharide syrup and the shishito peppers and cook over high heat for 2 minutes, shaking the pot to glaze everything.
Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Add the oligosaccharide syrup at the end. Put in at the start, it scorches during the braise and turns bitter.
Keeps for up to 5 days in the fridge. The seasoning soaks in further as it cools.
Boiled quail eggs braised alongside make this a good lunchbox side.
